blocks.content: Quiz: Why did the SpeedBlip build use 7 separate Claude Code chunks instead of one large prompt?
Tap an option below to answer:
Claude Code has a character limit that prevents long prompts from being submitted
Claude Code can process long prompts. The chunking decision was strategic, not a technical workaround for a character limit.
Claude Code can process long prompts. The chunking decision was strategic, not a technical workaround for a character limit.
Each chunk creates a testable checkpoint and a git commit, so the build never moves forward from a broken state
Correct. Chunking gives you verification checkpoints and safe rollback points. If Chunk 5 breaks something, you can roll back to the Chunk 4 commit and try again without losing earlier work.
Correct. Chunking gives you verification checkpoints and safe rollback points. If Chunk 5 breaks something, you can roll back to the Chunk 4 commit and try again without losing earlier work.
Smaller prompts are always cheaper to run than large prompts
Cost is not the reason for chunking. The methodology is about build quality and control, not API cost optimization.
Cost is not the reason for chunking. The methodology is about build quality and control, not API cost optimization.
Claude Code performs better on UI code than on logic code, so they need to be separated
Claude Code handles both UI and logic well. The chunking separation is about independent testability and scope clarity, not AI performance differences.
Claude Code handles both UI and logic well. The chunking separation is about independent testability and scope clarity, not AI performance differences.
